hook.text: Two billion people suffer micronutrient deficiencies — biofortification breeds vitamins and minerals into staple crops.

buildup.text: HarvestPlus developed iron-rich pearl millet and zinc-rich rice — conventional breeding guided by nutritional targets.

discovery.text: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes provide beta-carotene — adopted by 10 million households in sub-Saharan Africa.

twist.text: Biofortification works only if farmers adopt and consumers accept the new varieties — taste and yield must match.

climax.text: CRISPR now accelerates biofortification — editing existing varieties to accumulate more micronutrients directly.

punchline.text: Breed the nutrition in — biofortification feeds and nourishes at once.

quiz.question: What is biofortification?
options: Adding vitamin supplements to processed food products
Breeding or engineering staple crops to contain higher levels of essential micronutrients
Spraying crops with mineral solutions to increase their nutrient content
